description: The plot illustrates how three accuracy-related metrics (Final Acc, Δ Acc, and Initial Acc) vary as a function of Initial Confidence. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately 0.95 to 0.99 with labeled ticks at 0.95, 0.96, 0.97, and 0.99 (a point is also plotted between 0.97 and 0.99). The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 with regularly spaced tick labels at 0.2 intervals. The “Final Acc” series is a solid blue line with circular markers and vertical error bars; it is about 0.90 at 0.95, about 0.86 at 0.96, about 0.89 at 0.97, rises to roughly 0.93 at the intermediate point between 0.97 and 0.99, and is about 0.88 at 0.99. The “Δ Acc” series is an orange dashed line with diamond markers and vertical error bars; it is about 0.90 at 0.95, about 0.86 at 0.96, about 0.88 at 0.97, about 0.87 at the intermediate point, and declines to about 0.75 at 0.99. The “Initial Acc” series is a green dash-dot line with square markers and vertical error bars; it is near 0.00 at 0.95 and 0.96, around 0.01 at 0.97, increases to about 0.05 at the intermediate point, and reaches about 0.13 at 0.99, with the largest error bar visible at 0.99.
